subject.title: [Bug]: 2 codex accounts, same machine, same docs, one has balloon startup cost

question: Should default Codex app-server state for OpenClaw-authenticated stdio runs become account-scoped, and if so should existing per-agent codex-home state be migrated, intentionally reset, or left for manual cleanup?
rationale: The likely fix is not just a line-level bug repair: moving CODEX_HOME changes native Codex auth, sessions, SQLite/log state, plugin cache/data, and operator diagnostics paths for existing users.

options.title: Account scope with explicit upgrade behavior
options.body: Use auth-profile-scoped Codex homes and document or implement the chosen migration/reset/cleanup path before closing this issue.

options.title: Keep per-agent state and add diagnostics
options.body: Preserve the current storage boundary and instead improve detection, reset guidance, or diagnostics for cross-account state pollution.

options.title: Defer until live proof
options.body: Wait for maintainers or the reporter to provide a live two-account run before choosing the storage boundary change.

recommendation.title: Account scope with explicit upgrade behavior
recommendation.body: Use auth-profile-scoped Codex homes and document or implement the chosen migration/reset/cleanup path before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work and current blame show this owner closest to the Codex app-server storage boundary and user-home/product behavior.
